slot.brief: Rank a set of given radicals (benzylic, allylic, tertiary, methyl) by stability; straightforward compare-and-rank with resonance reasoning.

stem: Arrange the following free radicals in decreasing order of stability: benzyl, allyl, tert-butyl and methyl.

verdicts.working: Benzyl and allyl radicals are resonance-stabilized, with benzyl more stable; tert-butyl is more stable than methyl due to hyperconjugation. Thus benzyl > allyl > tert-butyl > methyl.

working:
Benzylic and allylic radicals are resonance-stabilised; benzyl has greater delocalisation.\nAmong alkyl radicals, stability increases with substitution: $3^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{methyl}$.\nOrder: benzyl $>$ allyl $>$ tert-butyl $>$ methyl.

Independent check: Benzyl and allyl radicals are resonance-stabilized, with benzyl more stable; tert-butyl is more stable than methyl due to hyperconjugation. Thus benzyl > allyl > tert-butyl > methyl.
solution:
Resonance stabilisation makes benzylic and allylic radicals more stable; benzyl has greater delocalisation. Among alkyl radicals, stability increases with substitution due to hyperconjugation.
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2^\cdot > \text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2^\cdot > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^\cdot > \text{CH}_3^\cdot$$
